description: This plot illustrates the average correct gate rate as a function of the embedding layer, comparing different input types and datasets. The x-axis represents the embedding layer, with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30 and tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents the average correct gate rate, with a linear scale from 0 to 1.0 and tick labels at intervals of 0.2. Four lines are shown: Character Attention input (blue solid line), Character MLP input (blue dashed line), Wiki Attention input (red solid line), and Wiki MLP input (red dashed line). The Character Attention input line starts at around 0.2 at layer 0, peaks at approximately 0.8 at layer 5, drops to about 0.25 at layer 12, and then fluctuates between 0.6 and 0.75 from layer 20 to 30. The Character MLP input line begins at around 0.8 at layer 0, remains relatively stable until layer 10, then increases to around 0.9 at layer 15, and stays between 0.85 and 0.9 from layer 20 to 30. The Wiki Attention input line starts at around 0.25 at layer 0, peaks at approximately 0.8 at layer 5, drops to about 0.3 at layer 12, and then fluctuates between 0.55 and 0.7 from layer 20 to 30. The Wiki MLP input line begins at around 0.85 at layer 0, remains relatively stable until layer 10, then increases to around 0.9 at layer 15, and stays between 0.85 and 0.9 from layer 20 to 30. Shaded areas around each line represent the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions.
